content:
Updated 3 p.m. PT: Some T-Mobile users say iPhone service is coming back online, though others report it is still down.

T-Mobile's nationwide outage has left a large number of iPhone users seeing "SOS" in their status bar. Here's a full look at today's T-Mobile outage.

T-Mobile outage puts iPhones into "SOS" mode

Aggregated Downdetector stats show T-Mobile outages began around 4 p.m. ET / 1 p.m. PT and are impacting users across the country.

One Reddit thread has amassed thousands of complaints from affected T-Mobile users who say they can't make calls, send texts, or use mobile data. Other social platforms are also filling up with complaints from T-Mobile users.

Several of us here at 9to5Mac have also been impacted by today's T-Mobile outage and can't access any cellular connectivity on our iPhones.

Affected iPhone users will see an "SOS" icon in their status bar, which signifies that there is no cellular connectivity whatsoever. If you see this screen, that means T-Mobile is down in your area due to this outage. You can, however, still place emergency calls.

T-Mobile has yet to comment on the outage at this point, and it's unclear when service will be restored. Other carriers like Verizon and AT&T don't appear to be affected.

Are you affected by today's T-Mobile outage? Let us know in the comments.
